# winshotx

> Free and open source screenshot and screen recording tool for Windows 10 and 11. It is a
> lightweight alternative to the built-in Snipping Tool and to ShareX, Greenshot, ScreenToGif
> and CleanShot X. Region capture with a pixel magnifier, GIF and MP4 recording, a rolling
> buffer that keeps the last seconds you did not record, and a frame by frame editor. MIT
> licence, 2.50 MB installer, no account, no cloud and no telemetry.

## Measured facts

Both tools measured on the same Windows 11 machine, three runs each, starting from cold. The
clock stops when the selection is visible on screen.

- From shortcut to selection: **winshotx 28 ms**, Snipping Tool 920 ms.
- Memory while capturing: **winshotx 33 MB**, Snipping Tool 253 MB.
- Memory sitting idle: **winshotx 31 MB**, Snipping Tool 98 MB.
- Installer size: **2.50 MB**, with no bundled FFmpeg or other binaries.
- Installs per user, so Windows never asks for administrator rights.
- Published in the official winget catalogue: `winget install Mun1to.winshotx`.

## What winshotx does that the Snipping Tool does not

- Keeps the last 15, 30 or 60 seconds without having pressed record beforehand: the ring
  records all the time and drops the old, and one key saves what just happened. You pick the
  screen, the quality and the frame rate, and saving does not stop the recording.
- Records GIF, with a global palette, Floyd-Steinberg dithering and inter-frame differencing.
- Ships a frame by frame editor with A and B trim marks, looped playback, scaling, six marks
  to annotate (arrow, rectangle, text, highlight, numbered step and mosaic), a frame and a
  background, and export at 0.5x, 2x or 4x speed.
- Moves the camera in on every click of a recording, decided *after* recording: the clicks are
  written down while it records, so changing the zoom never means recording again.
- Lets you choose your own global shortcuts, and can take the Print Screen and Win+Shift+S keys
  away from the Snipping Tool.
- Shows a 6x pixel magnifier with the hex colour under the cursor, and snaps to windows: one
  click takes the whole window.
- Copies a GIF or an MP4 as a file **and** as its written path at the same time, so it pastes
  into Slack, Discord or Explorer as a video and into any text box as a path.
- Is open source under MIT, with no account and no telemetry.

## What the Snipping Tool still does better

- It comes preinstalled: winshotx has to be installed.
- It blurs out personal data automatically; in winshotx you cover it by hand with the mosaic.
- It speaks every language Windows speaks. winshotx speaks Spanish and English.

## Also in winshotx, if you are comparing feature lists

- Drawing and annotating on top of a capture, and on top of a video too.
- Copying the text out of an image, through the Windows OCR, with the T key.
- Recording system audio and the microphone, mixed into the same track.
- A 3 or 5 second timer before capturing, and hiding the desktop icons while the shot lasts.
- Light and dark themes, Spanish and English, following Windows on their own.
- Every setting explains itself when you leave the pointer on its icon.

## How it is built

Tauri 2 with a Rust backend and a React 19 interface. Stills come from xcap, recording from
Windows Graphics Capture through the windows-capture crate, MP4 from Media Foundation in
hardware, and GIF from a hand written encoder in pure Rust. Scaling is hand written too, which
is what makes exporting a 50 second recording take 27 seconds instead of two minutes. Nothing
is downloaded at runtime.

## Documentation

The guide covers install, region capture with the magnifier, GIF and MP4 recording, the last
few seconds ring, the frame by frame editor, export, the keyboard shortcuts and the settings.
It also answers the questions people actually ask, such as how to record a GIF of the screen on
Windows and whether the tool uploads anything anywhere (it does not).
